findings.mechanism: The genitive plural completes Rabb's construct relation, making the plurality what the Lord owns, governs and tends rather than a separate spatial setting for praise.
findings.reader_payoff: The last word defines what the title is Lord of.
findings.containment: QAC 1:2:4 is the worlds word; analysis 1:2:4 is Rabb. The accepted alignment, not matching numeric position, controls the reading.

epistemic.reason: The supplied surface, accepted alignment and cited local word evidence support this bounded relation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Evren ve içindeki yaratılmış varlıkların tamamı tek bir bütün olarak adlandırılır.
branch_activations.carrier: The noun denotes created beings as a whole.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Rabb demands the governed domain supplied by this dependent.
branch_activations.activation: The lexical whole fills the construct relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The entire created field falls within the title's stated lordship.
branch_activations.boundary: The noun is neither a free adverb of location nor the abstract state of knowing.

findings.title: worlds as recognizable signs
findings.claim: The created worlds can also be heard as distinguishable orders through which their caring Lord becomes recognizable and praise becomes informed recognition.
findings.mechanism: Al-alamin's created-classes sense and explicit sign-bearing rationale meet Rabb's care and hamd's recognition of worth. A distinct order can indicate the Lord to whom it belongs; recognizing that indication gives the opening praise an epistemic dimension.
findings.reader_payoff: The cosmic scope also becomes a field in which the praise-recipient can be recognized.
findings.containment: Al-alamin continues to mean worlds/created classes. Knowing and marking are relational resonances, not substitute dictionary translations; no specific landmark, revelation, or exhaustive proof is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The primary created-domain sense and sign-bearing naming rationale are explicit; their reciprocal epistemic effect is an interpretive local contact.

branch_activations.boundary: The naming rationale is explanatory evidence, not an independently demonstrated cosmological argument.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi bilme, tanıma ve gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavrama durumu bilgisizliğin karşıtıdır.

findings.title: plural distributes lordship
findings.claim: Al-alamin distributes the single Lord's relation across many communities or classes of created beings; the supplied rational-plural construal makes communal plurality audible within that comprehensive reach.
findings.mechanism: A plural dependent meets the singular title Rabb, extending the same governing relation across differentiated groups. The lexicon allows the whole creation and each created class to be named as a whole.
findings.reader_payoff: Universal lordship preserves plurality within its scope instead of making all beings one undifferentiated realm.
findings.containment: The MP tag establishes masculine plurality, not by itself a semantic restriction to rational beings. The source's communal construal coexists with the all-creation range; neither is ranked or used to erase the other.

epistemic.reason: Plural morphology and lexical class/whole alternatives are explicit; rational plurality is a trusted source construal, not forced by the QAC tag alone.

findings.claim: The ending of al-alamin closes the ayah audibly at the same point that its plural domain completes the reach of lordship.
findings.mechanism: The supplied final -in sound coincides with the last genitive dependent. The reported sound variant changes phonetic realization while the plural referent and syntactic closure remain.
findings.reader_payoff: The scope reaches its completion in the same word that brings the utterance to rest.
findings.containment: Only the canonical supplied ending and the reported effect can be stated. No specific alternative pronunciation, rhyme scheme, or reciter attribution is reconstructed.

epistemic.reason: Local surface and closure are explicit; variant details and adjacent-ayah cadence are not supplied.

findings.title: praise as considered verdict
findings.claim: Praise belongs to Allah, the worshipped Lord of the worlds, and can be heard as a considered recognition that his governing relation is praiseworthy when encountered across its domain.
findings.mechanism: Hamd supplies praise opposed to blame and, through the related positive-finding sense, an evaluation reached through experience. Lillah gives that evaluation its devotional recipient; Rabb names the ownership and governing activity being evaluated, and al-alamin gives that activity its field. The movement is from general praise-attribution to a considered verdict about experienced lordship.
findings.reader_payoff: The declaration can affirm recognized worth rather than leave praise disconnected from the Lord's relation to the worlds.
findings.containment: The ordinary praise assertion remains complete. The experience-based evaluation is an attributed interpretation, not a finite testing verb, a reported experiment on God, or a claim that praise depends on successful human verification. The before/after is a reconstructed HFT reading shift, not a staged reader measurement.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus coordinates and branch semantics support the relation; experience-based evaluation remains analogical and the HFT reader identity is legacy_unbound.

findings.title: worlds under stagewise cultivation
findings.claim: The Lord of the worlds can be heard as continually tending, repairing and bringing differentiated created orders toward completion, with nourishment and growing up sharpening the developmental content of that care.
findings.mechanism: Rabb's formation/completion sense meets the created plural it governs; the supplied split-root growth sense adds feeding as cause and growing as result. Al-alamin's distinguishing-sign relation makes those developing orders recognizable, and hamd becomes the response to their sustained cultivation. Static ownership thereby opens into ownership exercised through development.
findings.reader_payoff: The worlds appear as a plurality under continuing care, with distinct forms and histories of maturation.
findings.containment: The title remains a noun of lordship and does not narrate a timetable. The split mapping does not establish that QAC's r-b-b and lexicon r-b-w are identical roots. Nourishment is an image sharpened by the mapped branch; no assertion that every world is a biological child or crop follows. Completion describes the process's direction, not an already perfect cosmos.

epistemic.reason: Local attachment and core nurture semantics are grounded. The explicitly supplied split-root mapping and legacy HFT developmental synthesis are preserved with qualification.

findings.title: care cultivates recognition
findings.claim: The worlds can become a field of distinguishing signs through which caring lordship is known and praised; the related image of a God-knowing teacher who develops others' knowledge clarifies how care and growing recognition can belong together.
findings.mechanism: Al-alamin opens the created domain toward knowing and distinct signs. Rabb's nurturing relation meets that intelligible domain, while the related rabbani branch joins knowledge of God with teaching others by small steps. That human pedagogical relation supplies an analogy for care cultivating recognition; hamd's experience-based positive-finding sense then gives recognized signs an evaluative outcome. The shift is from a total collection of worlds to a legible field through which the Lord can be recognized.
findings.reader_payoff: Care can develop understanding as well as sustain existence, and praise can arise through that developing recognition.
findings.containment: Rabb remains Lord, not the human rabbani scholar. The analogy preserves the scholar's God-knowledge and actual teaching role rather than stripping the branch down to generic care. God is not said to acquire knowledge, and the ayah does not explicitly narrate lessons, a teacher or a human learner. The ordinary worlds and praise remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The knowing/sign and nurturing relation has direct packet support. The legacy HFT's pedagogical contact requires an explicit multi-step analogy preserving the restricted human scholar form.

findings.title: ultimate credit and derived favor
findings.claim: Assigning praise as due to Allah, the Lord of all worlds, can relativize a human benefactor's claim to own another's gratitude absolutely: provision received through others remains within the named Lord's encompassing care.
findings.mechanism: The related hamd idiom describes a person pressing favors upon someone to claim personal credit. Here the independent li-attribution directs ultimate praise to Allah, while Rabb's caring relation to the worlds supplies benefaction and recipient dependence. Comparing those directions yields an inverse social reading: a derivative favor need not make its giver the ultimate holder of praise. Need and favor remain distinct aspects; no literal knot is inferred.
findings.reader_payoff: The attribution can be heard as freeing gratitude from an unlimited personal claim by an intermediate benefactor, while ordinary thankfulness remains available.
findings.containment: The human credit-claim idiom is not the canonical al-hamdu lillah construction; its lexical boundary explicitly excludes that construction. It survives solely as the HFT's bounded inverse analogy activated by praise-attribution and nurturing lordship. No human coercer, specific debt, literal knot, ban on gratitude to people, or guaranteed social liberation is stated by this ayah.

epistemic.reason: The local attribution and care are grounded. The legacy HFT social reversal survives only as an explicitly inverse analogy preserving the person-directed idiom's form restriction and separate need/favor readings.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Praise to the Lord can relativize claims to absolute personal credit made through favors.
branch_activations.boundary: This branch is restricted to a person-directed idiom and explicitly excludes al-hamdu lillah as its lexical use; the activation is an inverse analogy, never a translation or predicate of divine coercion.

findings.title: Definiteness carried through the construct
findings.claim: The ayah presents definite praise and definite worlds, while the article-less Rabb gains a determinate relation through its attachment to those worlds and to the divine name.
findings.mechanism: The two visible al- prefixes mark the praise topic and the final domain. Between them, li- binds the named recipient and Rabb's construct relation connects that recipient to the definite plural. The absence of an article on Rabb therefore does not introduce an indefinite second lord.
findings.reader_payoff: The short sentence holds determinate praise, a named recipient and a determinate domain together; a translation can conceal how the Arabic makes those relations fit.
findings.containment: This is grammatical definiteness, not a claim that the two articles have identical semantic functions or that an article alone proves numerical exhaustiveness. The packet's all-worlds scope remains the semantic baseline.

epistemic.reason: The two article prefixes are supplied in focus_surface_evidence; the accepted name-title-domain attachments explain the article-less construct head.

findings.title: care as abundant water provision
findings.claim: The Lord's sustaining care for the worlds can be imagined through abundant provision: plentiful gathered water and a well rich in water make the cared-for domains perceptible as places where sustaining supply is available.
findings.mechanism: Rabb's ordinary nurturing relation is the entry point. Its root-family gathered-water image meets the separate al-alamin root-family image of a water-rich well; the shared water abundance fits the independent Lord-domain care relation. The contact gives a concrete provisioning image to care for the worlds while keeping Lord and worlds as their ordinary meanings.
findings.reader_payoff: The breadth of sustenance acquires a concrete image of available supply, alongside the developmental and epistemic readings.
findings.containment: This is a local root-mediated analogy, not a lexical translation of Rabb as water or al-alamin as wells. The water lexemes differ from the canonical forms, and trusted word analysis explicitly treats water as locally inactive at the ordinary word-sense level. No water infrastructure, rain, irrigation, freshwater requirement, actual geographical well, or recurring surah system is asserted. The sea alternative remains available in the lexicon but is not activated by this well-specific contact.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies both exact water-image facets on distinct focus-root carriers and the ordinary care relation. Their combination is an independent author inference, with canonical form differences and word-analysis nonactivation kept visible.
